skipped_reasons: PAT-OPERATION-PRECONDITION-SCOPE (canonical pattern) was applied, not extended: avg was correctly decided to need no PreconditionError by examining its own domain (denominator is the constant 2, no undefined native-semantics input region), matching the pattern's decision rule rather than copying div/mod by analogy (Brief constraints cites the node id; verification-report.json W1 check 2 explicitly asserts PreconditionError is never thrown for avg). This is the pattern working as designed on a second operation (pow, then avg) -- it is confirmation of an existing canonical node's applicability, not a new choice/exception/boundary, so it does not clear the non-triviality bar for a new or superseding candidate.

LES-CONTRACT-TESTS-MISS-HTTP-DISPATCH (canonical lesson) was proactively satisfied, not extended: the Brief built R5 (extend src/server.ts's OPERATIONS whitelist) and R7 (a dedicated real HTTP-level test for op:avg, distinct from R6's module-level contract tests) directly from this lesson, and verification-report.json W1 check 2 confirms an automated tests/http/server.test.ts test dispatches op:avg through the OPERATIONS whitelist and asserts a 200 response -- the exact HTTP-dispatch-reachability gap the lesson warns about was avoided by construction. This is the lesson doing its job (informing the Brief so the gap never recurred), which is what the node existing is for; it does not by itself yield new durable information, so no new/superseding node is proposed.

Watch-item (not promoted to a candidate): the lesson's body also recommends confirming HTTP-test sensitivity with a mutation spot-check (temporarily drop the new op value from the whitelist, rerun, confirm only the HTTP test fails, then restore). verification-report.json's W1 checks record only the positive-path HTTP test (op:avg -> 200 {result}), not an executed mutation spot-check for R5/R7 -- so the lesson's stated verification step was followed in spirit (an automated HTTP test now exists, an improvement over add-power-operation's manual curl smoke test) but not to the letter this time. This is a single occurrence, not yet a recurring pattern across changes, so it does not clear the universality/stability bar for a new lesson or a supersedes revision; flag for harvest reconsideration if a future change also has an automated HTTP test that skips the mutation spot-check and it turns out to matter (e.g. a whitelist regression that a non-mutation-tested HTTP test would not have caught).

No new concept/vocabulary candidates: `solidsdd-kg promote suggest --json` returned 8 contract_vocabulary gaps (MemoryResponse, ErrorResponse, Calculator, Memory, Operation, CalculateRequest, CalculateResponse, MemoryValueRequest) -- all pre-existing OpenAPI/OCL schema names untouched by this change, none newly introduced or newly at risk of scope confusion by adding avg. The op enum's avg value itself and PreconditionError's absence for avg were already flagged as sub-bar watch-items in knowledge-consult.md (recur across only 2 changes so far: add-power-operation, add-avg-operation) -- still short of the 'recurs across multiple changes / contracts' stability bar for a concept node; not proposing here to avoid inventing a node 'for completeness'.

verified_at freshness: knowledge.md defines no repeated-confirmation or usage-counter mechanism for existing nodes -- verified_at is set once at promote/apply time and is consumed only by check's FR-210 staleness threshold (warn when older than N days), not as an accumulating confirmation log. Both applicable nodes already carry verified_at: 2026-08-13 (set at their add-power-operation apply) which is today's date for this change too, so no staleness condition exists to address and no bump action was taken or is warranted by this change succeeding.
